svg.title: AC power as a function of time
svg.desc: The power P = I0V0 sin²(2πft) delivered to a resistance by an AC source, versus time t. Because the voltage and current are in phase, the power is never negative: it oscillates between zero and I0V0 at twice the source frequency. The average power, shown dashed, is ½I0V0. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: AC power in a pure resistor
V and I are in phase: peaks 10 V and 2 A, frequency 1 Hz. P = VI is nonnegative, oscillates at twice
the frequency, and averages 10 W. Two seconds shown.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
